page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, no margin notes. Running head at top right: "CHRISTI NATALI. Pars II.", page number 107 at top right. A four-line italic verse passage set off in the middle of the page. Catchword and signature at the foot.

main_text.p: terquam[?] enim quod Josephus non dixerit totale fuisse illud lunæ deliquium, nec ab eo certo mensi allegetur, varii sunt characteres historici, cum quibus hinc sententiam nunquam conciliare potuerunt viri doctissimi.

A. Historia Caji, in consessu Romano (Herodis testamentum excutiente) præsentis, qui anno Jul. xliv Orientem adiit, prohibet annum Herodi emortualem ad sequentem, ærae Jul. xlv, protrahere. Cajus inquam, Agrippæ ex Julia Augusti filia natus anno Jul. 25 ab avo suo deductus fuit, simulque consul destinatus post quinquennium anno Jul. 41. Augusto xii & L. Corn. Sulla coss. Nata sunt abhinc diffidia Parthorum cum Romanis, & quidem illo biennio, quod inter xii Augusti consulatum & xiii annis nempe Jul. 42. 43. intercessit, hinc anno 44 Jul. Augusto xiv, & Plauto Sylvano coss. Cajus occasione motus Parthici in Syriam tanquam rector Orientis missus est. Fuit annus ille Jul. xliv in historia valde nobilis ex Naumachiæ spectaculo, quod exhibuit Augustus. Jam vero, eo tempore, quod Naumachiæ spectaculum sequebatur proximè, Cajum abiisse in Orientem patet ex Ovidio, libro de arte amandi, eoque carmine, quod in Naumachiæ istius solemnia scripsit, in quo Cajum, tanquam in Orientem adversus Parthos proximè profecturum ita celebrat.

p.i: Ecce parat Cæsar, domito quod defuit orbi Addere, nunc Oriens ultime noster eris. Auspicius armisque patris puer arma movebis, Et vinces armis auspiciisque patris.

main_text.p: Hoc idem quoque confirmat Paterculus, itineris Caji in Orientem ipse quoque comes, qui cum Naumachiæ

page.notes: Page is clean and legible except the first word of the page, "terquam", which is partly lost in the gutter and is marked [?]. The verse lines read "Auspicius" in print (kept as printed; the scan shows "Auspicius armfque"). Printed "Aufpicius" with long s was rendered as plain s. The printed "Et vinces armis aufpiciisque patris" was copied with plain s. Roman numerals and dates were copied as printed in lower case where they appear that way. Italic was applied to names and the verse; the scan's italic extent is approximate.
